description:
We are Cosmodyne, a technology-driven team passionate about web development, software engineering, data analysis, and space exploration. We believe that technology and scientific innovation can make complex challenges easier to understand and solve.

Our goal is to develop an intuitive lunar landing-site navigation and mission-planning platform that simplifies the evaluation and comparison of potential landing locations on the Moon, particularly in the challenging south polar region.
summary:
I developed the Lunar Landing Site Navigator, an interactive mission planning dashboard designed to solve the complex challenge of selecting safe landing locations at the lunar South Pole.

The application directly addresses the challenge by integrating NASA's JPL Horizons API with high-resolution lunar Digital Elevation Models (DEM). It calculates 360-degree horizon profiles to identify terrain occlusion, mapping exactly when the Sun and Earth are visible across a 29.5-day lunar cycle. Planners can scrub through an interactive timeline, compare sites or launch dates side-by-side, and save custom coordinates to a persistent site library.
details:
What it does:
An interactive web dashboard for lunar South Pole mission planning. Users select a site on the map to instantly generate a 360-degree terrain horizon profile. It integrates NASA's JPL Horizons API to plot Sun and Earth positions across a 29.5-day interactive timeline, visually highlighting the overlapping windows for solar power and communication.

Benefits & Impact:
It replaces fragmented, manual data analysis with instant visual feedback, preventing catastrophic power or communication blackouts. By enabling side-by-side comparisons of different sites and launch dates, it allows planners to rapidly assess trade-offs and adjust schedules, accelerating and de-risking future Artemis missions.

Tools & Software Used:

  • Framework: Next.js, React, TypeScript.
  • Mapping & Math: OpenLayers, Proj4.
  • Data Sources: NASA JPL Horizons API, LRO Digital Elevation Model (DEM).
  • Processing: Recharts, geotiff.
  • Infrastructure: Cloudflare R2 (for hosting the 180MB DEM file), Vercel.

Creativity & Factors Considered:
Creativity comes from translating dense, raw scientific data into an intuitive UI—such as visualizing overlapping safe zones as a glowing "Golden Window." We prioritized performance by hosting the massive 180MB DEM on Cloudflare R2 to bypass serverless limits, and optimized our API calls to respect NASA's rate limits while keeping the interface highly responsive.
